name: Time zones converter
seoTitle: Time zones converter Calculator — Formula, Units & Example
seoDesc: Time zones converter: a free conversion calculator that walks you through 52 values, with the formula spelled out and a worked example.
summary:
The Time zones converter returns your result from the 2 fields on the form. No sign-up, no page reload, and the relationship behind it is printed below.

That makes it useful for a recipe, a shopping list, a travel plan or a form that asks for a unit you do not use. Nothing is submitted anywhere: the arithmetic runs in the page you are looking at.

sections.title: How does the Time zones converter calculator work?
sections.html:
The Time zones converter takes the values in the form, applies the relationships described below and reports every result it can derive from them.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case; then you give the dates it asks for.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• A single on/off switch — tick it for “Display all time zones”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
  • A date and a time of day. Use the picker; the answer is recalculated the moment the date changes, and the count is done date-to-date rather than by subtracting timestamps.

1 field on this form is a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Time zones converter calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

UTC/GMT=CET ÷ WAT − 3600
UTC/GMT=EET ÷ UZ1 − 7200
MSK/EAT=UTC ÷ GMT + 10800
SMT/AZT/GET/AMT/MUT=UTC ÷ GMT + 14400
PKT/YEKT/MVT=UTC ÷ GMT + 18000
UTC/GMT=OMSK ÷ BST − 21600

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Time zones converter earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Reading a recipe written in units you do not use
  • Filling in a form that asks for imperial or metric values
  • Converting a figure someone quoted you so you can compare it

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Dates are compared date to date in your own time zone, so a daylight-saving change will not shift the count by a day.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Time zones converter calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for a few values, which is 2 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Time zones converter calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. The calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.
